articles.title: Gordon Ramsay's 15-Minute Bolognese Pasta Recipe
articles.summary: A simple and satisfying pasta dish that can be cooked in under 15 minutes using just a handful of ingredients from Gordon Ramsay's Ultimate Cookery Course series.
articles.content: Gordon Ramsay's 15-minute pasta recipe has become a staple in my household, much to my family's delight. The dish, which is part of his tagliatelle with sausage Bolognese recipe, requires just a handful of ingredients and can be cooked in under 15 minutes. This simplicity is what makes it so appealing to home cooks like me who are looking for quick yet satisfying meals. My family's love affair with this pasta dish began when we stumbled upon Gordon Ramsay's Ultimate Cookery Course series, which features 100 essential recipes that the chef demonstrates on screen. The show originally aired in the UK in 2012 and has since become a favorite comfort watch of ours. One episode caught our attention, and it was then that we discovered Ramsay's tagliatelle with sausage Bolognese recipe. This particular dish became our go-to comfort dinner during the early days of the pandemic. The reason for its enduring popularity lies in the fact that it is easy to make and requires minimal ingredients. The five main components of this recipe are dried tagliatelle pasta, sausages, tomatoes, half an onion, and a few cloves of garlic. To start making Gordon Ramsay's 15-minute Bolognese pasta, I chop up some essential ingredients - onions, garlic, and parsley. The prep time for this dish is remarkably short, taking me around five minutes or less to get everything ready before cooking begins. While the original recipe doesn't include Italian parsley, I like adding it if I have some on hand as it adds a burst of freshness and color to the dish. I also dice up some tomatoes - in my case, cocktail tomatoes which provide a nice juiciness to the Bolognese sauce. The beauty of this recipe is its adaptability to your preferences and what you already have in your kitchen. On this particular night, I used cocktail tomatoes, which add a touch of sweetness and moisture to the sauce. Before cooking, I also prep the sausage by peeling off the casings and crumbling the meat - Ramsay recommends slicing each sausage down the middle to make this process easier. Once my pasta is in a pot of salted boiling water, I sauté some onions in a pan until they're softened before adding the rest of the ingredients. The addition of garlic and parsley is next on the agenda as I prepare Gordon Ramsay's Bolognese pasta recipe. I carefully add the ingredients to the pan where the onions are already softened. As per Ramsay's advice, I let the garlic and onions "sweat until they're soft" before introducing the meat into the mixture. This step is crucial in developing the flavors of the dish. I use a spatula to break down the sausage while mixing everything together, ensuring that all the ingredients are well combined. Seasoning with salt and pepper at this stage also enhances the overall flavor profile. The addition of chopped tomatoes is followed by a can of crushed tomatoes, which I believe helps to create a richer and more textured sauce. This was a modification we made to the recipe after trying it twice without the extra can of tomatoes, and it's since become an integral part of our Bolognese pasta dish. As the sauce simmers away, I check on the pasta's doneness by catching one of the pappardelle ribbons in a ladle, running it under cold water for a few seconds before biting into it to assess its firmness. As the sauce simmers away, I add two ladlefuls of pasta water to it, which is a crucial step according to Gordon Ramsay's recipe. The starch from this added pasta water helps thicken the Bolognese sauce and makes it stick better to the noodles. Once I've done that, I remove the sauce from the heat while my pappardelle continues cooking. After draining the pasta, I throw the cooked noodles into the pan with the sauce and mix everything together thoroughly. The result is a meaty and rich Bolognese sauce that's perfectly balanced by the flavors of the sausage and other ingredients. articles.content: In a post-championship celebration, Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy was caught making some candid comments on a hot mic while talking to first baseman Jake Bauers, who is set to enter free agency after a standout season. Bauers had a remarkable year with the Brewers and was named NLCS MVP. However, it's his previous stint with the New York Yankees that seems to be at the center of Murphy's remarks. The comment in question appears to take a swipe at the Yankees' culture during Bauers' time there. The comment drew criticism from those who assumed Murphy was criticizing the entire Yankees organization. It's worth noting that the Yankees had a disappointing season, finishing with an 82-80 record and missing out on the playoffs. In an effort to clear up any misunderstandings, Murphy reached out to Yankees general manager Brian Cashman immediately after learning about the incident. He explained his intentions in a recent interview, stating that he had been jokingly referencing his past interactions with Bauers during their time together at the Yankees. When speaking with Cashman, Murphy reportedly clarified that he was not making a comment about the current state of the Yankees organization but rather referencing his own lighthearted banter from previous years. In hindsight, it's clear that Pat Murphy's comment about Jake Bauers' free agency was taken out of context. When managers and players engage in casual conversations without realizing they're being overheard, unintended remarks can be misconstrued. Murphy's statement was not a criticism of the Yankees organization as a whole, but rather a lighthearted observation about teams with high-paid, long-term contracts struggling to gel on the field. This perspective is shared by many fans, including those from the Bronx, who would agree that Murphy's assessment has some merit. However, what sparked controversy was the implication that players receiving large paychecks become self-centered and less inclined to contribute to team goals. This notion is not entirely supported by recent trends in baseball, where high-paying teams like the Dodgers have successfully balanced individual salaries with championship success. The Dodgers' back-to-back World Series titles serve as a counterexample to this narrative, highlighting that even teams with significant individual contracts can still achieve collective greatness on the field. The apology from Brewers' manager Pat Murphy to Yankees' general manager Brian Cashman has been reported, following a comment made by Murphy that sparked controversy about free agency and player contracts. Murphy's remark was perceived as insensitive towards players who need to prioritize their financial security, particularly those with significant individual contracts. This perspective is rooted in the reality that MLB players have limited time to earn money due to their relatively short careers, making it crucial for them to maximize their earnings while they can. Murphy's comment seemed to dismiss this concern. The incident appears to be a minor blip on the radar, with some speculating that it may not lead to any significant repercussions or tension between the two teams. Unless Bauers, who was the subject of Murphy's comment, decides to speak out against him in the future, this controversy is likely to fade away without any lasting impact. articles.title: Crohn's Disease Patients May Experience Anxiety from Fiber-Rich Foods
articles.summary: Individuals with Crohn's disease may experience anxiety about consuming fiber-rich foods due to unpredictable tolerance levels.
articles.content: A significant number of people with Crohn's disease experience anxiety when thinking about consuming fiber-rich foods, due to their unpredictable tolerance levels. Certain foods that are high in fiber can be particularly challenging for individuals with the condition, even those that seem harmless like omelets or fruit smoothies. As a result, many people with Crohn's avoid fiber altogether, which is not uncommon given research suggesting they tend to consume relatively little of it, even during periods of remission. A 2015 study found that individuals with Crohn's averaged just 16 grams of fiber per day, well below the recommended daily intake for men of 38 grams. Experts caution against adhering to a low-fiber diet as a means of managing Crohn's symptoms, despite its potential benefits in reducing inflammation and improving gut health. Fiber is a type of carbohydrate found in plant-based foods that the body cannot fully break down or absorb. It resists digestion in the stomach and small intestine, and depending on its type, it is either partially or fully fermented by gut bacteria in the colon. There are two main types of fiber: insoluble and soluble. Each has distinct functions and benefits for overall health. Insoluble fiber passes through the gastrointestinal tract largely intact, adding bulk to stools and helping to regulate bowel movements. Foods rich in insoluble fiber include pear and apple skins, raspberries, wheat bran, leafy greens like kale and collard greens, nuts, seeds, and legumes. Fiber intake during a Crohn's disease flare can be a delicate matter, requiring careful consideration of individual tolerance levels. Registered dietitians suggest that amounts should gradually increase as symptoms subside, but it's essential not to overdo it initially. Anya Argosh, MS, RD, advises against consuming excessive fiber when experiencing active symptoms, recommending moderation instead. Dahlia Marin, RDN, LD, CGN, cautions that eliminating all fiber may not be necessary during a flare, especially for those without strictures in the gastrointestinal tract. Historically, people with Crohn's were often advised to follow a low-fiber diet when experiencing diarrhea, abdominal pain, or increased bowel movements. When dealing with a stricture, it's crucial to modify eating habits to minimize the risk of an obstruction. This involves consuming softer foods or adjusting textures, limiting insoluble fiber sources, and chewing thoroughly. It's essential to note that individuals with strictures have unique dietary needs, and a personalized plan should be developed in collaboration with a healthcare provider. The importance of individualized planning cannot be overstated, as people respond differently to various diets. A healthcare provider can work with the individual to create a tailored approach, taking into account their specific nutritional requirements and health status. This collaborative effort enables individuals to make informed decisions about their diet and avoid exacerbating symptoms. Some healthcare professionals recommend a low-FODMAP diet during active flare-ups of Crohn's disease. This short-term strategy may help alleviate symptoms triggered by fermentable carbohydrates that can be challenging for the gut to process. High-FODMAP foods, such as certain beans, legumes, cabbage, cauliflower, garlic, and onions, can cause discomfort in some individuals. A low-FODMAP diet is often employed on a temporary basis in people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) to identify symptom triggers. This approach may also benefit individuals with Crohn's disease who experience IBS-like symptoms. By temporarily removing high-FODMAP foods from the diet, it's possible to determine which specific foods are contributing to discomfort. When increasing fiber intake with Crohn's disease, a gradual and cautious approach is recommended. Introducing too much fiber at once can worsen symptoms, leading to bloating and discomfort. To avoid this, individuals should start by incorporating small portions of well-tolerated fiber-rich foods throughout the day, then gradually expand their fiber intake. A "low and slow" approach to adding more fiber to the diet is essential for managing Crohn's disease. This involves pacing fiber introduction, rather than forcing it, as suggested by healthcare professionals. By spreading out high-fiber foods and gradually increasing the types and amounts consumed, individuals can minimize discomfort and promote a healthier digestive system. A multi-step approach to increasing fiber intake is recommended by some experts, starting with soft fruits, vegetables, and grains that are easy on the digestive system. This may include foods such as potatoes, white rice, and bananas, which can be gradually replaced with harder-to-digest options like salad, seeds, corn, celery, and dried fruit. It's also essential to remember that hydration levels should increase alongside fiber intake to prevent constipation and soften stools. As individuals adjust to a higher-fiber diet, they may experience some discomfort, but spreading out high-fiber foods over time can minimize this effect and promote a healthier digestive system. Incorporating more plant-based foods into one's diet is generally the best way to increase fiber intake, as these foods not only provide vitamins and minerals but also antioxidants that support overall health and may help reduce inflammation. Fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and other plant-based foods offer numerous benefits beyond just fiber content, making them an ideal choice for those looking to boost their fiber levels naturally. A registered dietitian can play a crucial role in helping individuals with Crohn's disease manage their condition through diet. They can assess nutrient deficiencies and develop a personalized eating plan that takes into account any specific dietary needs or restrictions. Identifying trigger foods is another key aspect of managing Crohn's disease, and a registered dietitian can help with this process as well. However, it's essential to note that triggers can vary significantly from person to person, making it challenging to pinpoint them. The presence of strictures, post-surgical dietary needs, or other complications related to Crohn's disease may also require the expertise of a registered dietitian. In some cases, individuals with Crohn's may need to undergo trial and error to determine which foods work for them and which ones don't. It is vital that individuals with new or worsening symptoms seek medical attention, particularly if they experience persistent abdominal pain, frequent diarrhea, blood in their stool, unexplained weight loss, fatigue, or vomiting. articles.summary: A new film project has emerged from the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on global society. The movie, titled DreamQuil, is the brainchild of artist Alex Prager and her sister Vanessa, who drew...
articles.content: A new film project has emerged from the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on global society. The movie, titled DreamQuil, is the brainchild of artist Alex Prager and her sister Vanessa, who drew inspiration from a meme that went viral during lockdown. Prager reveals in an interview that she had been eager to direct movies for some time, and this idea was the catalyst for her first feature film. She shares that her sister joined forces with her to develop the concept into a screenplay, which they wrote during the pandemic's isolation period. The story follows Carol, a woman living in a dystopian near-future plagued by pollution and stress. Her life is dominated by virtual reality escapism and advertisements bombarding her screens, until she discovers the DreamQuil program, a temporary reprieve from the pressures of her world. Carol's decision to enroll in the DreamQuil treatment has far-reaching consequences for herself and those around her, including her strained relationships with her husband and son. The film paints a vivid picture of a hyper-polluted society where daily life feels overwhelming. The film DreamQuil is a cinematic representation of a society overwhelmed by pollution, where daily life feels suffocating. The movie's narrative takes its cue from a COVID-19 meme that sparked Alex Prager's creative imagination. This artistic departure marks the first foray into filmmaking for the photographer. Prager's background in photography has been marked by unconventional routes. At 47, she dropped out of high school and learned the art form through self-study. Her training was put to use capturing everyday life in her Los Feliz neighborhood, where people became the subjects of her lens. Her photographs are characterized by sweeping compositions that evoke a distinct California aesthetic, reminiscent of Hollywood's Golden Age and film noir. Close-ups with vibrant color palettes sit alongside images of crowded streets filled with surreal and uncanny elements, showcasing Prager's mastery over composition and color. The meticulous composition of DreamQuil's 84-minute runtime is a testament to Alex Prager's skill as a filmmaker. She storyboarded every frame before bringing her cinematographer on board, ensuring that each moment was carefully crafted. Prager drew inspiration from classic films such as Douglas Sirk melodramas and Technicolor classics, incorporating vibrant colors into her work. A striking example of this can be seen in the lush field of poppies that pays homage to The Wizard of Oz. The use of color is a deliberate choice for Prager, who believes it can convey complex emotions and ideas. In the film, the red dress worn by Carol serves as a symbol of humanity, representing blood and life. The themes explored in DreamQuil are complex and multifaceted, tackling issues that resonate deeply with audiences today. The film's narrative delves into the constraints of femininity and marriage within a patriarchal society, echoing familiar tropes seen in classic movies like The Stepford Wives. However, Prager sisters' vision takes a more incisive approach by critiquing corporatism and AI-driven manipulation. Advertisements play a pivotal role in this narrative, bombarding Carol with tailored appeals that prey on her vulnerabilities. This portrayal serves as a commentary on the exploitation of personal data and the impact of corporate control. Prager's aim was to write a script that specifically addressed concerns around data privacy, drawing inspiration from the work of B.F. Skinner, whose philosophy was first applied in Las Vegas's casinos to create an immersive and addictive experience. The internet has since been transformed into a similarly gamified platform, leveraging tactics like constant notifications and personalized recommendations to keep users engaged. The seemingly benevolent company at the center of Alex Prager's latest film, DreamQuil, appears to be a force for good, providing relief from stress and anxiety through its marketing efforts. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that this altruistic image is actually a ruse. Prager explores the darker side of human nature in her work, examining the thin line between artificiality and reality through vibrant, populous portraits. In DreamQuil, she critiques the ways in which our personal data is exploited for profit, highlighting the insidious nature of this practice as we willingly surrender our privacy. articles.title: Africa Becomes Significant Hub for Synthetic Drugs Production
articles.summary: Recent discoveries of methamphetamine laboratories in several African countries have raised concerns that Africa is emerging as a significant hub for synthetic drugs.
articles.content: Africa's reputation as a transit point for international drug trafficking networks is slowly changing as the continent becomes increasingly involved in the production of illicit drugs. Recent discoveries of methamphetamine laboratories in several countries, including Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, and Mozambique, have raised concerns that Africa is emerging as a significant hub for synthetic drugs. This shift in the global drug trade has been facilitated by transnational criminal networks and clandestine laboratories capable of supplying both local and international markets. The involvement of African countries in the production of synthetic drugs has gained momentum over the past few years, with several high-profile discoveries of methamphetamine labs across the continent. In Nigeria, for instance, authorities have uncovered multiple labs, including one described as the largest clandestine methamphetamine laboratory ever discovered in the country. The dismantling of this lab by Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has brought international attention to the issue, with concerns about the scale and sophistication of African-based drug production operations. The discovery of massive quantities of methamphetamine and precursor chemicals in Nigeria has sparked concerns about the country's growing role in the global drug trade. Officer raids have uncovered an estimated $363 million worth of illicit substances, highlighting the scale of production taking place on African soil. The sheer volume of seized materials has left authorities scrambling to keep pace with the rapidly evolving situation. Methamphetamine labs are being dismantled at an alarming rate, raising questions about local consumption levels. Nigerian authorities have long been aware of small-scale meth laboratories operating within the country's borders, but recent operations suggest a more sophisticated network is taking shape. DW correspondent Olisa Chukwumah notes that it's no longer just a matter of seeing drug production in movies, it's now a harsh reality on Nigerian soil. Experts say Nigeria's shift from being a transit nation to a consumer nation has been gradual, with the country now discovering its own role as a major player in methamphetamine production. Dokun Adedeji, co-founder of the Compassionate Care Recovery Initiative, notes that dozens of smaller labs have been uncovered over the years, with multiple states implicated in meth production. The rise of synthetic-drug production in West Africa is closely tied to growing local consumption and expansion of illicit markets. This trend has devastating consequences for individuals and communities, as described by Dokun Adedeji. Substance abuse is a major contributor to school dropouts, family breakdowns, mental health issues, and rising crime rates. Families often struggle to seek help due to stigma and fear of public judgment, making it difficult for them to openly discuss their struggles with addiction. Young people are disproportionately affected by drug-use disorders, with 34% of those receiving treatment in Africa under the age of 25. The increasing prevalence of synthetic marijuana in Nigeria is a growing concern, prompting NGOs to launch awareness campaigns on university campuses where drug use is becoming more visible. These efforts aim to educate students about the dangers of synthetic marijuana and encourage them to seek help if they or someone they know is struggling with addiction. A lack of coordinated policies at the national level has hindered efforts to address the issue, leaving civil society groups to fill the gap through their awareness work. Experts argue that punishment-based approaches often drive users underground, making it harder for authorities and healthcare providers to identify and support those in need of help. To effectively combat synthetic marijuana use, UNODC and civil society groups advocate a broader response that incorporates prevention programs, rehabilitation services, and regional cooperation across West Africa. This includes strengthening national policies on substance abuse, implementing workplace drug prevention programs, and increasing regional coordination to tackle the issue more effectively. articles.title: Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel Sign with Big Records at Age 15
articles.summary: The duo began performing together as children, eventually landing a record deal and releasing their first single.
articles.content: Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel, one of music's most iconic duos, have a remarkable history that spans from their childhood in Queens, New York to their rise to global fame. The two men grew up in the same neighborhood, attended the same schools, and shared a passion for popular music. Their early experiences laid the foundation for their future success. As children, Simon and Garfunkel began performing together, starting with a sixth-grade production of Alice in Wonderland. This marked the beginning of a long-standing musical partnership that would go on to shape the course of pop history. In their teenage years, the duo's talents caught the attention of record labels. By the time they were 15, Simon and Garfunkel had written and sold their first single, "Hey, Schoolgirl, and signed with Big Records, marking a significant milestone in their careers. Simon and Garfunkel's musical journey is well-documented, but one aspect of their story remains relatively unknown, the origins of their most successful song as a duo. Despite their later success, the lead vocalist of this iconic track had initial reservations about performing it. As their music career took off, Simon & Garfunkel continued to balance education with creative pursuits. The duo's early success was marked by their first professional contract with Big Records, secured at just 15 years old. Their subsequent collaboration as Tom & Jerry led to the writing and release of songs, including Hey, Schoolgirl, which they had written and sold earlier. This experience laid the groundwork for their future work together. After Simon graduated from Queens College, he reconnected with Garfunkel, who was studying at Columbia University. The duo reunited under a new moniker, Kane & Garr, and began performing in Greenwich Village. Their music caught the attention of Tom Wilson, an A&R man from Columbia Records, leading to their signing with the label. This move marked a significant turning point in their career, paving the way for future success. The pair's debut studio album, Wednesday Morning, 3 A.M., was released by Columbia Records in October 1964. The album received positive reviews and set the stage for their subsequent releases. Following the success of their first few albums, Simon & Garfunkel went on to release three more well-received LPs: Sounds of Silence," "Parsley, Sage, Rosemary and Thyme," and "Bookends. These albums solidified their status as two of the most successful artists of their time. The album Bridge Over Troubled Water has undergone a significant transformation over time. Initially met with mixed reviews upon its release in 1970, it is now widely regarded as one of the finest folk-rock works of that decade. Several songs from the album have become deeply ingrained in popular culture. Cecilia" and "Bye Bye Love are just two examples of the timeless tracks that continue to resonate with audiences today. The album also features a haunting rendition of the Peruvian classic, El Cóndor Pasa. A surprising aspect of Bridge Over Troubled Water is its title track's almost-alternate history. Despite becoming an iconic hit by reaching number one on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, it was nearly very different from what we know today. Paul Simon drew inspiration for Bridge Over Troubled Water from a gospel song called Oh Mary Don't You Weep, performed by the legendary group the Swan Silvertones. According to Simon's own recollection, he would often listen to this record upon returning home and it would stay with him, influencing his work. Simon took the melody of Oh Mary Don't You Weep and adapted it to incorporate gospel chord changes. This creative process reflects the artist's interest in exploring different musical styles and traditions. The impact of Simon's unique approach can be heard in the final version of Bridge Over Troubled Water, which features a distinctive blend of folk, rock, and gospel influences. The influence of gospel music on Simon's songwriting is evident in Bridge Over Troubled Water. The track was inspired by the classic gospel number Oh Mary Don't You Weep performed by the Swan Silvertones. When Simon first played his demo to Art Garfunkel, he reportedly didn't want to sing lead vocals. According to Simon, his partner felt that he should have taken on the task himself. This initial reluctance was a surprising twist given Garfunkel's distinctive contribution to the final version of the song. In hindsight, it seems clear that Simon was initially hesitant about having Garfunkel sing lead on Bridge Over Troubled Water". Simon has stated that many times he wished he had taken on the responsibility himself. This would have been a significant departure from the eventual arrangement. It's worth noting that decades later, Garfunkel claimed that his initial hesitation was an act of generosity. He felt that the song was so strong that it should be led by Simon, rather than himself. Paul Simon had written a song so powerful that it sparked an unexpected debate within the duo. Initially, Art Garfunkel felt that the song was too strong to be led by him and instead should be spearheaded by Simon. This bold gesture of generosity on Garfunkel's part may have been genuine, but its nature remains unclear even decades later. Regardless of his true intentions, it is intriguing to consider an alternate reality where this iconic number might not have featured Garfunkel's voice as the lead singer. articles.title: Historic Upsets Mark 2026 Midterm Elections in the US
articles.summary: The midterm elections saw significant shifts in power with Democrats regaining control of both chambers of Congress after flipping seven Senate seats.
articles.content: A historic night of upsets and milestones marked the 2026 midterm elections in the United States. For the first time in American history, a Black woman was elected governor, with Keisha Lance Bottoms winning in Georgia. The elections saw significant shifts in power, with Democrats regaining control of both chambers of Congress after flipping seven Senate seats. This included Republican strongholds where the party had not held sway for decades. The outcome has sent shockwaves across the country as voters chose new leaders and broke down long-standing barriers. In other states, notable firsts were achieved, including Michigan electing its first Muslim senator, Abdul El-Sayed, and New Hampshire its first openly gay male senator, Chris Pappas. Texas also saw a significant milestone with the election of its first Latina governor, while Florida elected its first Black governor, Republican Byron Donalds. The midterm elections have yielded a record number of historic victories for Democrats across the country. In Nevada, Attorney General Aaron Ford made history by becoming one of the first Black governors elected in the state's history. This achievement is significant not just for its novelty but also for the fact that it marks a shift in the state's political landscape. In Wisconsin, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley has been elected as the state's first Black governor. Crowley's victory is part of a broader trend of increasing diversity in politics and reflects the changing demographics of the state. His election sends a strong signal about the growing influence of minority groups in Wisconsin's electoral process. The Democratic Party's gains extend beyond gubernatorial elections, with notable victories in Senate seats. In Ohio, former state health director Amy Acton has been elected as governor, marking the first time a woman has held the office. This achievement is significant given the relatively small number of female governors in the United States. In South Carolina, pediatrician Annie Andrews made history by becoming the first Democrat to win a Senate election since 1998 and the state's first-ever female senator. Her victory highlights the changing electoral landscape in traditionally Republican strongholds like South Carolina, where Democrats are increasingly making inroads. In Alabama, Democrat Allison Montgomery made history by becoming the state's first openly transgender lawmaker after defeating Republican incumbent Phillip Rigsby in her bid for office. Montgomery, a software engineer and prominent LGBTQ+ rights advocate, campaigned on key issues such as public education, healthcare, and affordability despite facing relentless attacks from her opponent on her gender identity. In another notable victory, 30-year-old Beau Bayh won the race for Indiana's secretary of state, marking the first time a Democrat has held statewide office in the state since 2012.
